history.summary: The Mahalakshmi Temple on Bhulabhai Desai Road (Breach Candy, Cumballa Hill) enshrines the Tridevi — Goddess Mahalakshmi flanked by Mahakali and Mahasaraswati, adorned with gold bangles, nose rings and pearl necklaces. Legend links its founding to the Hornby Vellard project connecting Mumbai's islands: after the sea wall failed twice, chief engineer Ramji Shivji Prabhu is said to have dreamed of the goddess, recovered her idols from the Worli creek, and enshrined them on the hillock, after which construction succeeded. CONFLICT (verify): sources date the temple variously to 1761–1771, c. 1785, and 1831 — the temple trust's own website says 1831 and credits merchant Dhakji Dadaji; treat the founding date as disputed. The temple is managed by the Shri Mahalakshmi Temple Trust and is famed for the sunrise rays falling directly on the idols during Navratri. Coordinates are approximate (street-level match off Bhulabhai Desai Road).

name: Mahalakshmi Temple
town_description: Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra and India's financial and entertainment capital, spread across seven islands on the Konkan coast along the Arabian Sea. Home to well over 12 million people, it blends colonial-era landmarks with one of the country's densest clusters of historic temples and pilgrim sites. It is connected nationally and internationally through Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, two major railway zones, and an extensive suburban rail and road network.
